newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macquarie considers share buy-back - paper.
newsitem.headline: Macquarie considers share buy-back - paper.

text.p: Investment bank and broking house Macquarie Bank Ltd would announce at this week's annual meeting it is considering a share buy-back to soak up A$150 million of excess capital, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Tuesday.

"A buyback to absorb the entire A$150 million would involve about 12 million shares, or about eight percent of the investment bank's stock, and reduce Macquaries's tier one capital from 13 percent to nine percent, a level with which ratings agencies have told the bank they are comfortable," the newspaper said.

"Sources confirmed that the bank was considering reducing tier-one capital to these levels, although no detailed buy-back plan had been hatched and other avenues of capital reduction would be examined," the newspaper said.
Macquarie chairman David Clarke told a news conference on June 2 after Macquarie's annual result that there was every chance Macquarie would have to a look at a capital return.

This was because the Reserve Bank was expected to reassess its capital adequacy rules for market risk, increasing Macquarie's measured capital strength or capital adequacy to above 16 percent, Clarke said then.
Macquarie would also announce at its annual meeting on Wednesday that it would consider expanding the employee option scheme and introducing tougher performance hurdles.
Macquarie's shares closed down 13 cents at A$12.76 on Monday.
